en.text:
Today’s M&A briefing — 8 deals, the strategies behind them · 15 October 2026

🔹 Mubadala Capital (investment arm of Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund) finalizes the acquisition of Clear Channel Outdoor (leading US out-of-home advertising network: urban billboards) — $6.2bn.
Clear Channel delists from the New York Stock Exchange. Wade Davis, founder of ForgeLight and architect of the Univision-Televisa merger, takes over as group CEO; John Halley becomes Chief Commercial Officer.
Our view: A Gulf sovereign wealth fund acquires out-of-home advertising as an audience infrastructure asset resistant to ad-blocking and screen fragmentation, betting that physical attention in cities will appreciate as online attention fragments.

🔹 Leonardo gets green light to acquire Iveco — €1.7bn.
— manufacturer of land military vehicles — for €1.7 billion.
Our view: Strategic interpretation: Leonardo consolidates its capabilities in land combat systems at a time when European defense budgets are sharply increasing.

🔹 Ithaca Holdings acquires Bumble (austin-listed dating app) — $1.3bn.
Common shareholders receive $6.05 per share, more than double the recent price. Founder Whitney Wolfe Herd will remain involved; Gupta and Hegeman will become co-CEOs. This is Ithaca Holdings' first investment.
Our view: Ithaca bets that the Bumble brand and its mission are worth more than the listed market was willing to pay, by acquiring an undervalued asset to restructure it away from quarterly pressure — the open question is whether the sector's contraction is cyclical or structural.

🔹 DigitalBridge, TD Greystone Infrastructure and L&G consortium (infrastructure investors) acquires VodafoneZiggo's passive telecom tower assets (passive telecom towers and sites in the Netherlands) — €669m.
Closing is expected before the end of 2026. Proceeds from the sale will reduce VodafoneZiggo's debt, as part of a €1.2 to €1.4 billion divestment program aimed at preparing Ziggy Group's IPO in Amsterdam in mid-2027.

🔹 Symbotic (robotic and AI-powered systems for supply chains of major US retailers) acquires cellumation GmbH (omnidirectional sorting surface composed of independent cells).
cellumation retains its name, its Bremen headquarters, and its customer base. This is Symbotic's third acquisition after ARMS Innovations and Fox Robotics. Integration into Symbotic's product roadmap aims for denser warehouses and a reduced footprint.

🔹 Dekuple Group (international communication and data marketing group listed in Paris) takes a majority stake in SAY (omnichannel marketing and communication agency founded in 2004).

🔹 Clessidra Private Equity (italian private equity fund) acquires Citres (condiments and preserves, pesto, salsa and derivatives).

🔹 BOWI (shell and interior fitting group, carpentry, layout) acquires Savouret Galien (nantes-based shell carpentry).

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — 7 deals, the strategies behind them · 15 October 2026

🔹 Atoms (robotics and industrial automation, turnkey professional kitchen operator, ProKitchens for restaurateurs) — $1.7bn.
Atoms is founded by Travis Kalanick, co-founder of Uber. ProKitchens is part of the Atoms Food division alongside CloudKitchens, with active sites in Paris, Marseille, Lille, Lyon, Madrid, Barcelona, Milan, Lisbon, Warsaw, and Amsterdam.
Investors: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), lead investor; Uber, Bain Capital, Fifth Wall and other institutional investors. Ben Horowitz joins the board of directors.
Our view: ProKitchens is not just a kitchen rental but a shared food logistics infrastructure whose value grows with network density; Uber's presence in the round signals a direct interest from the delivery platform in densifying the ghost kitchen offering.

🔹 Flying Whales (development of a heavy cargo airship, LCA60T for freight transport in hard-to-reach areas, production site in Laruscade, Gironde) — €90m.
This round brings the total funding raised to nearly €400 million out of a planned budget of €500 million. CMA CGM is the world's leading shipping company.
Investors: CMA CGM via Pulse, its fund dedicated to energy transition and logistics decarbonization. The Nouvelle-Aquitaine Region has been a shareholder since the beginning.
Our view: CMA CGM is not making a technological bet: it is investing in a logistical capacity complementary to its core maritime business.

🔹 Epyr (high-temperature thermal storage using refractory bricks for industrial clients) — €15m · Series A.
Founded by Léa Dardenne and Bastien Oggeri. The model utilizes low or negative-priced electricity hours to charge refractory bricks that release heat on demand. The installation at Papeco is presented as France's largest thermal storage facility.
Investors: SlateVC, lead investor; AENU, Daphni, OVNI, WEPA Ventures, Aurum Impact.
Our view: Epyr arrives at the right time: France has already recorded more hours of zero or negative-priced electricity this year than in all of 2025, and this surplus without an outlet is exactly what Epyr monetizes by storing it as heat for gas-consuming industries.

🔹 JamboSec (AI-based cybersecurity, threat detection, risk management calibrated for businesses in emerging African markets, based in Nairobi) — $12m · Series A.

🔹 Fragment (double-entry accounting tools enabling developers to integrate AI agents into billing and payment flows without risk of error) — $12m · Series A.

🔹 Spash (video and statistical analysis technologies for leisure sports, padel, tennis, 5-a-side football for sports centers, created) — €2m.
Spash equips nearly 450 sports centers.

🔹 Revelo (modular low-code SaaS platform for automated data collection, analytics, reporting, and workflow management for compliance) — $300k · pre-seed.

fr.text:
Levées de fonds : les 7 opérations chiffrées de l'édito du 15 octobre 2026.

🔹 Atoms (𝑟𝑜𝑏𝑜𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑠𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒, 𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑢𝑖𝑠𝑖𝑛𝑒𝑠 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑓𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑐𝑙𝑒́ 𝑒𝑛 𝑚𝑎𝑖𝑛) — 1,7 Md$.
Atoms est fondé par Travis Kalanick, co-fondateur d'Uber. ProKitchens fait partie de la division Atoms Food aux côtés de CloudKitchens, avec des sites actifs à Paris, Marseille, Lille, Lyon, Madrid, Barcelone, Milan, Lisbonne, Varsovie et Amsterdam.
Avec : Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), chef de file ; Uber, Bain Capital, Fifth Wall et autres institutionnels. Ben Horowitz rejoint le conseil d'administration.
Point de vue : ProKitchens n'est pas une simple location de cuisine mais une infrastructure logistique alimentaire mutualisée dont la valeur croît avec la densité du réseau ; la présence d'Uber au tour signale un intérêt direct de la plateforme de livraison à densifier l'offre de restaurants fantômes.

🔹 Flying Whales (𝑑𝑒́𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑑'𝑢𝑛 𝑑𝑖𝑟𝑖𝑔𝑒𝑎𝑏𝑙𝑒 𝑐𝑎𝑟𝑔𝑜 𝑙𝑜𝑢𝑟𝑑, 𝐿𝐶𝐴60𝑇) — 90 M€.
Ce tour porte le total des financements mobilisés à près de 400 M€ sur un budget prévu de 500 M€. CMA CGM est le premier armateur mondial de transport maritime.
Point de vue : CMA CGM ne fait pas un pari technologique : il investit dans une capacité logistique complémentaire à son cœur de métier maritime.

🔹 Epyr (𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑐𝑘𝑎𝑔𝑒 𝑡ℎ𝑒𝑟𝑚𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 ℎ𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑒 𝑡𝑒𝑚𝑝𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒 𝑝𝑎𝑟 𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑟𝑒́𝑓𝑟𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑠) — 15 M€ · Série A.
Fondée par Léa Dardenne et Bastien Oggeri. Le modèle exploite les heures d'électricité à prix bas ou négatifs pour charger des briques réfractaires qui restituent la chaleur à la demande.
Avec : SlateVC, chef de file ; AENU, Daphni, OVNI, WEPA Ventures, Aurum Impact.
Point de vue : Epyr arrive au bon moment : la France a déjà enregistré cette année plus d'heures d'électricité à prix nul ou négatif qu'en 2025 entier, et ce surplus sans débouché est exactement ce qu'Epyr monétise en le stockant sous forme de chaleur pour des industriels gaziers.
